result.summary: Bumps the minimum supported GCC compiler version from 12.1 to 13.1, enforcing C++20 `std::format` support during CMake configuration. It updates CI environments to use GCC 13 and Ubuntu 24.04, removes the NetBSD cross-build job from the GitHub Actions matrix, and replaces an example `strprintf` invocation with `std::format` in a benchmark.
result.problem: GCC 12 lacks support for C++20 `std::format`, preventing developers from using standard text formatting across the codebase and blocking the project's eventual migration to C++23.
evidence: PR description: "For this bump, only C++20 `std::format` will become available, but this bump should also pave the way for C++23."
Commit ee8d04cd15 demonstrates the payoff by migrating `src/bench/wallet_migration.cpp` from `tinyformat` (`strprintf`) to `std::format`.
result.changed_since_previous: Removed the NetBSD cross-compilation job from the GitHub Actions matrix due to unstable upstream package availability, and dropped manual `-Werror` flags from the native previous-releases CI script.
result.card: PR 36042 raises the minimum supported GCC compiler version from 12.1 to 13.1, enforced in CMake via a feature check for C++20 std::format. This enables codebase adoption of std::format and paves the way for C++23, while requiring users on older Linux distributions lacking GCC 13 to build using Clang or alternative toolchains. CI configurations are updated to Ubuntu 24.04, and the NetBSD cross-compilation task is removed from GitHub Actions.

risk.why: Mistakes in CMake compiler feature detection or toolchain requirements could break builds for supported platforms and developers building from source.
